i_title: Night Shift. On-call agents that never solve the same incident twice, even when the other shift solved it. Against a wiki that holds every on-call note, it solves repeat pages in 3.3 steps instead of 5.9 and at 42 percent of the tokens, with 2 to 9 points less accuracy, and its Postgres ledger cuts wrong fixes by 27 to 52 percent against memory alone.
i_p1: Shift A fixes the 2 a.m. page. The fix lives in their own notes.
i_p2: The next night, shift B gets the same page, and starts from the wiki again.
i_p3: And sometimes a remembered fix stops working, but people keep applying it.
i_a1: Night Shift runs the two shifts as two Meko members who share one datapack.
i_a2: Each page is traced in a Meko conversation. A verified fix becomes a private memory and a postmortem.
i_a3: At the end of the night, the curator promotes approved fixes to the team's collective knowledge. In production a person approves them; this benchmark approves automatically. When the agent gives up, the engineer's own fix goes in the same way.
i_a4: A Postgres ledger is joined with every memory hit, and records whether each remembered fix still works.
i_a5: Now, the same 40 pages, answered twice by the same local model.
b_INC-01: Left: the whole runbook is in the prompt. Right: Night Shift searches Meko first. Night one, and neither side has seen this page.
b_INC-09: A few nights later, shift A gets a page it already solved. Night Shift finds its own fix in Meko in 1 step. The runbook lane is still investigating.
b_INC-12: Now shift B gets a page that shift A solved. The curator promoted that fix, so B finds it in 1 step.
b_INC-24: A trap. The alert looks like the first page, but the cause has changed.
b_INC-30: Another trap. The remembered heap fix fails, so the Postgres ledger retires it. The agent gives up, and the on-call human's fix goes into Meko.
b_INC-34: Watch the right lane: the old API key fix fails once, then Night Shift finds the real cause and remembers it.
b_INC-36: Shift B now gets the cause from INC-30. The human's fix was shared overnight, so Night Shift needs 1 step, while the runbook lane keeps searching.
b_INC-39: Shift B gets the cause that was learned on INC-34. The corrected fix is already shared, so Night Shift needs 1 step.
d_end: Totals for all 40 pages, and below them what the team learned, promoted, and retired in the ledger.
p_1: The same run in the Meko portal: one datapack for the whole team.
p_2: Context efficiency: tokens sent per query, against a full context baseline.
p_3: Collective learning: conversations become memories, and promoted memories become shared knowledge.
p_4: Two members. Shift A owns the datapack and curates. Shift B is a contributor, so only A can promote.
p_5: Shared knowledge: the team runbook, plus the fixes the curator promoted.
p_6: Each newly learned fix also left a postmortem artifact, from both shifts.
p_7: Self-learning: Meko scores how well each search matched. The librarian answers the weak ones and replays them.
o_res: In the run you just watched, on repeat pages, Night Shift resolved 96 percent, against 56 for the runbook, with 72 percent fewer tokens. Offline, sharing matters: 89 percent shared, 72 with private memory only, and 71 from the agents' own fixes without any human notes. Traps stay hard: 33 percent, against 33 for the runbook. Across all 3 live seeds, repeat pages went from 56 to 92 percent; most of that is the on-call notes reaching the next shift, since a wiki given the same notes does about as well.
o_end: The code, the replay dashboard, and every recorded run are on GitHub. No paid model API was used.
